newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain's share index reaches new record high.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain's share index reaches new record high.

text.p: Bahrain's share index climbed nearly six percent to a new record high this week in brisk trade focused on bank shares, official figures showed on Thursday.
The Bahrain Stock Exchange (BSE) said the index ended the week at 1,539.23 points, up from 1,454.86 points a week earlier.
Trading volume rose to 27.4 million shares from 22.8 million shares the previous week. The value of shares traded also climbed to 5.3 million dinars ($14 million) from four million dinars last week.
Both the index and trading volume reached the highest levels since the bourse was established eight years ago.

BSE said Bahrain International Bank (BIB) shares continued to dominate trade. More than 13.5 million shares worth 2.2 million dinars were traded, up from 11.9 million shares worth 1.6 million dinars last week.

BIB shares, also traded on the Kuwait Stock Exchange, rose 14 fils on the BSE this week to close on Thursday at 159 fils per share, after gaining 34 fils last week amid speculation in both Bahraini and Kuwaiti bourses.
Al-Ahli Commercial Bank shares came next with 2.2 million shares worth 646,039 dinars changing hands. Its share prices rose 18 fils to 294 fils on Thursday.
Shares of 21 firms out of 39 registered on the bourse were traded in 445 transactions, the bourse said.
Bahrain's bourse is open to nationals in Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman, Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates. Some firms are also open to foreign investors.
